theory.intro: The angles $30^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ come up so often that their ratios are worth knowing exactly, without a calculator. Each exact value comes from one of two special right-angled triangles. The boundary angles $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$ complete the set.
facts: $\tan90^{\circ}$ is **undefined**, because the adjacent side shrinks to $0$ and $\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$ has no value.
To find an unknown side, choose the ratio linking it to the known side and the given angle, substitute the exact value, then solve.
steps: Choose the ratio linking the known and unknown sides
Substitute the exact value of the ratio

workedExamples.question_text: State the exact values of $\cos60^{\circ}$, $\sin0^{\circ}$ and $\tan45^{\circ}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Read the corresponding entries in the exact-value table.

$\cos60^{\circ}=\frac12$

$\sin0^{\circ}=0$

$\tan45^{\circ}=1$

$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$

At $90^{\circ}$, the numerator is $1$ and the denominator is $0$. Division by zero is undefined, so $\tan90^{\circ}$ is undefined.

Find the hypotenuse using Pythagoras.

$\begin{align*}h^2&=2^2+2^2\\h^2&=8\\h&=2\sqrt2\end{align*}$

The opposite and adjacent sides are both $2$.

$\begin{align*}\sin45^{\circ}&=\frac{2}{2\sqrt2}\\&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\cos45^{\circ}&=\frac{2}{2\sqrt2}\\&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac22\\&=1\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}h^2+3^2&=6^2\\h^2&=27\\h&=3\sqrt3\end{align*}$

For $30^{\circ}$, the opposite side is $3$, the adjacent side is $3\sqrt3$ and the hypotenuse is $6$.

$\sin30^{\circ}=\frac36=\frac12$

$\cos30^{\circ}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$

$\tan30^{\circ}=\frac3{3\sqrt3}=\frac1{\sqrt3}$

For $60^{\circ}$, the opposite and adjacent sides exchange roles.

$\sin60^{\circ}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$

$\cos60^{\circ}=\frac36=\frac12$

$\tan60^{\circ}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{3}=\sqrt3$

Sine links the opposite side $x$ to the hypotenuse.

$\begin{align*}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{12}\\\frac12&=\frac{x}{12}\\x&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Cosine links the adjacent side $y$ to the hypotenuse.

$\begin{align*}\cos30^{\circ}&=\frac{y}{12}\\\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&=\frac{y}{12}\\y&=6\sqrt3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Tangent links the opposite side $x$ to the adjacent side $9$.

$\begin{align*}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{9}\\\frac1{\sqrt3}&=\frac{x}{9}\\x&=\frac9{\sqrt3}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Cosine links the adjacent side to the hypotenuse.

$\begin{align*}\cos30^{\circ}&=\frac9h\\\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&=\frac9h\\h\sqrt3&=18\\h&=\frac{18}{\sqrt3}\\h&=6\sqrt3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Use tangent to find each height.

$\begin{align*}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac{BC}{8}\\BC&=8\tan45^{\circ}\\BC&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{BD}{8}\\BD&=8\tan60^{\circ}\\BD&=8\sqrt3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Subtract the smaller height from the larger height.

$\begin{align*}x&=BD-BC\\&=8\sqrt3-8\\&=8(\sqrt3-1)\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text: State the exact value of $\tan90^{\circ}$, or write that it is undefined.
foundation.solution_text:
$\tan90^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$
At $90^{\circ}$ the adjacent side is $0$, and dividing by $0$ has no value.
$\tan90^{\circ}$ is undefined.

The angle $45^{\circ}$ has opposite $1$, adjacent $1$ and hypotenuse $\sqrt{2}$.
$\sin45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\cos45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\tan45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\dfrac{1}{1}=1$

From the $30^{\circ}$ angle, the opposite is $1$, the adjacent is $\sqrt{3}$ and the hypotenuse is $2$.
$\sin30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{2}$
$\cos30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\tan30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

development.solution_text:
From the $60^{\circ}$ angle, the opposite is $2\sqrt{3}$, the adjacent is $2$ and the hypotenuse is $4$.
$\sin60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\cos60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2}$
$\tan60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}=\sqrt{3}$
